title: The upper unitriangular group scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $n\geq0$ an integer. Index $n\times n$ matrices [def-weil-matrix] by $I=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and put $J=\{(i,j)\in I^2:i<j\}$ and $P=k[x_{ij}:(i,j)\in J]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $M$ be the matrix over $P$ with $M_{ii}=1$, $M_{ij}=x_{ij}$ for $i<j$, and $M_{ij}=0$ for $i>j$. Define algebra maps $\Delta:P\to P\otimes_kP$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], $\epsilon:P\to k$, and $S:P\to P$ by
$$\Delta(x_{ij})=\sum_{l\in I}M_{il}\otimes M_{lj},\qquad\epsilon(x_{ij})=0,\qquad S(x_{ij})=\left(\sum_{r=0}^{n-1}(I_n-M)^r\right)_{ij}.$$
The upper unitriangular group scheme $\mathcal U_{n,k}$ is the affine $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}P$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with the multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms induced by these three maps. These specified maps uniquely determine a group-scheme structure [def-sc-group-scheme]. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, its points are precisely the upper triangular matrices over $A$ with diagonal entries $1$, with matrix multiplication. For $n=0$ this is the trivial group scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$.
